use_when: a dedicated autonomous software-engineering runtime is the missing capability
the project needs a reusable software-agent SDK or isolated workspace execution
automation should run through a dedicated coding-agent environment rather than the current IDE
avoid_when: the existing AI IDE already executes the route reliably
the task is a small repository-local edit
adding another general coding runtime would only duplicate capability

notes: For the OpenHands CLI, current upstream recommends `uv tool install openhands --python 3.12`.
For a minimal local SDK integration, current upstream documents `pip install openhands-sdk openhands-tools`.
Add `openhands-workspace` and `openhands-agent-server` only when sandboxed/remote execution is actually required.
Do not install both CLI and SDK surfaces by default; choose the interface that closes the route capability gap.

credentials: LLM provider/API credential or another upstream-supported authentication method for the selected mode
permissions: filesystem/shell access bounded to the selected workspace
Docker/remote execution permissions only when the chosen workspace mode requires them
external service permissions only for explicitly enabled tools

checks: run one bounded representative repository task in the selected OpenHands surface
confirm workspace isolation and tool permissions match the intended boundary
run project acceptance/regression checks outside the agent loop before adopting changes
verify OpenHands closed the original execution gap rather than merely duplicating the current host

steps: uninstall the selected OpenHands CLI/SDK packages with the package manager that installed them
remove sandbox/server infrastructure created only for the integration

warnings: OpenHands is a general coding-agent platform/runtime; AAOP should keep routing, policy, and provider selection outside it.
Broader workspace/server modes materially increase permission and infrastructure surface compared with the local SDK/CLI.
